apps.name: Activepieces
apps.what_is_sent: A daily snapshot of the deployment shape such as replica counts, resource sizes, versions and settings. Product analytics adds tracked events and in-app page view counts.

disable.instructions: Turn off the deployment snapshot in the UI under Platform Admin > Account > Configurations. It does not read AP_TELEMETRY_ENABLED.

disable.name: AP_TELEMETRY_ENABLED
disable.note: Only seeds the product analytics setting the first time it is read. After that the UI toggle controls it.

apps.notes: The deployment snapshot is documented as on by default. The docs do not state the default for product analytics or name the destination host.

apps.name: Appsmith
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous navigation, click and successful backend-call events.
apps.still_sent: Keep-alive and server-setup pings are sent whether telemetry is on or off.
apps.notes: api.mixpanel.com is the endpoint shown in the sample payloads in the docs. It is shared with other products that use Mixpanel.

apps.name: Arize Phoenix
apps.what_is_sent: Basic web analytics about interactions with the Phoenix web interface. No trace or evaluation data.
apps.notes: PHOENIX_ALLOW_EXTERNAL_RESOURCES=false is meant for air-gapped installs and also blocks other external resources. The docs page does not name the destination host.

apps.name: Chatwoot
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymised metadata such as aggregate record counts, inbox and conversation type distributions and enabled integrations, sent periodically.
apps.notes: The docs say self-hosted installations periodically send this data and give the variable as the way to stop it. They do not use the word "default".

apps.name: CockroachDB
apps.what_is_sent: Obfuscated usage details, shared periodically by each node and by the DB Console.
apps.still_sent: On Enterprise Trial and Enterprise Free licenses the opt-out setting is ignored, so reporting stays on.

disable.instructions: With an Enterprise license only. Set COCKROACH_SKIP_ENABLING_DIAGNOSTIC_REPORTING=true before starting the first node, or run SET CLUSTER SETTING diagnostics.reporting.enabled = false; on a running cluster.

apps.notes: The environment variable is listed as a manual step because it only works with an Enterprise license, so its presence alone does not prove reporting is off. The docs do not name the destination host.

apps.name: Coder
apps.what_is_sent: Usage and deployment metadata such as feature and template details, plus the administrator's email. No secrets or end-user identities.
apps.notes: The docs page does not name the destination host.

apps.name: Directus
apps.what_is_sent: Usage data about your environment, used to gauge installation frequency, version fragmentation and user base size.
apps.still_sent: A one-time project owner registration is sent when an owner is first set. It is controlled separately by PROJECT_OWNER_ENABLED.
apps.notes: The docs add that whether telemetry can be disabled depends on your license.

apps.name: Documenso
apps.what_is_sent: App version, an installation ID and a node ID, sent on server startup and with a periodic heartbeat.
apps.notes: The docs say "our telemetry servers" without naming a host, so no destination is listed.

apps.name: Dozzle
apps.what_is_sent: The Dozzle version, deployment mode, enabled auth provider, feature flags, Docker Engine version and counts of hosts, containers and filters, with a random per-install ID. No log contents, container names or IP addresses.
apps.notes: The docs describe analytics as something you opt out of. They do not use the word "default".

apps.name: Firezone
apps.notes: Unverified. The source page could not be opened when this entry was written, so the default and the variable come from a search engine summary of that page. The image name was not checked either. That summary describes the legacy self-hosted release and says the variable turns off product telemetry. Whether it also covers package and firezone-ctl telemetry is not known.

apps.name: Forgejo
apps.notes: Unverified. The configuration reference has no telemetry or usage reporting setting, but no official page states outright that Forgejo sends none. What it does document is a version check that is on by default (cron.update_checker ENABLED = true) and queries a DNS TXT record on release.forgejo.org. The image names were not checked against an official compose file.

apps.name: Gitea
apps.notes: Unverified. The configuration reference has no telemetry or usage reporting setting, but no official page states outright that Gitea sends none. What it does document is a version check that is on by default (cron.update_checker ENABLED = true) and fetches https://dl.gitea.com/gitea/version.json.

apps.name: GitLab
apps.what_is_sent: Service Ping collects and sends a weekly payload to GitLab Inc.

disable.note: Run gitlab-ctl reconfigure afterwards. This also stops the setting from being changed in the Admin area.

disable.instructions: Or in the UI go to Admin > Settings > Metrics and profiling > Usage statistics and clear Enable Service Ping. Clear Enable version check there as well to stop the version check.

apps.notes: The docs describe usage statistics as opt-out on free GitLab Self-Managed instances. They do not state the default for paid tiers.

apps.name: Grafana
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous usage statistics.

disable.name: GF_ANALYTICS_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES
disable.note: Stops the check for new Grafana versions.

disable.name: GF_ANALYTICS_CHECK_FOR_PLUGIN_UPDATES
disable.note: Stops the check for new plugin versions.

apps.notes: The docs give the config keys and the GF_<SECTION>_<KEY> rule for environment variables. The variable names here follow that rule.

apps.name: Hasura GraphQL Engine
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous, aggregate usage statistics from the server, Console and CLI, such as object counts and error events.
apps.notes: The docs describe telemetry as something you opt out of. They do not use the word "default".

apps.name: Home Assistant
apps.what_is_sent: Only after you opt in. An installation identifier, the Home Assistant version, installation type and country code, plus optional usage details and counts.
apps.notes: Analytics is opt-in. The docs say nothing is sent unless you explicitly opt in, during onboarding or later under Settings > System > Analytics. The docs do not name the receiving host.

apps.name: Immich machine learning
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous ONNX Runtime metric data, sent to Microsoft by the bundled onnxruntime library.

disable.name: ORT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY
disable.note: Only needed on versions before v3.3.6. The image sets it itself from v3.3.6.

apps.notes: Caused by onnxruntime turning telemetry on by default in a recent release, so older Immich versions that bundle an older onnxruntime are not affected. phonehome cannot tell the version from a moving tag such as "release".

apps.name: Infisical
apps.notes: The docs give the default as true. They do not say what is sent or where.

apps.name: Jellyfin
apps.notes: The project states that Jellyfin has no tracking, phone-home, or central servers collecting your data.

apps.name: Kodus
apps.what_is_sent: One anonymous heartbeat per day with aggregated usage counters and runtime metadata. No code, identities or personal data.
apps.notes: The docs say each instance sends the heartbeat but not which container does it, so the variable is suggested for every backend container. The official compose file loads them all from the same env file.

apps.name: Langfuse
apps.what_is_sent: High-level aggregated usage metrics such as version, project and trace totals. No raw traces, prompts or email addresses.
apps.still_sent: Enterprise self-hosted telemetry is used for license compliance and cannot be disabled.

disable.name: TELEMETRY_ENABLED
disable.note: Set it on every Langfuse application container.

apps.name: Lightdash
apps.what_is_sent: Usage events tied to organization, project, user and content UUIDs, plus some resource titles, descriptions and short error messages. No SQL, query results or credentials.

disable.name: RUDDERSTACK_ANALYTICS_DISABLED
disable.note: Set it on every container that runs Lightdash code (backend, scheduler, workers).

apps.name: Grafana Loki
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous usage reports.
apps.notes: The opt-out is a command-line flag or a config key, not an environment variable, so phonehome detects the flag but cannot write a fix.

apps.name: Mattermost
apps.what_is_sent: Error and diagnostics reporting sends server errors and panics with no message content. The security update check sends the server version, edition, OS, database type and team and user counts once every 24 hours.

disable.instructions: In the System Console turn off Environment > Logging > Enable Diagnostics and Error Reporting.
To stop the security update check as well, turn off Environment > SMTP > Enable Security Alerts. You will then not receive security alerts.

apps.notes: The telemetry page gives only the System Console paths, so no environment variable is listed and phonehome cannot write a fix. It does not name the destination hosts.

apps.name: Meilisearch
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymized system, performance and usage metrics, sent in batches through Segment.
apps.notes: The docs name Segment as the collector but give no hostname, so no destination is listed.

apps.name: Metabase
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous, non-personal usage data such as in-product events, some performance data, the number and types of connected databases and counts of items created.

disable.name: MB_CHECK_FOR_UPDATES
disable.note: Stops the check for new Metabase versions.

disable.instructions: Or turn off "Anonymous tracking" under Admin > Settings > General.

apps.notes: The docs name Snowplow as the collector but give no hostname, so no destination is listed.

apps.name: n8n
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous usage telemetry, sent mostly at event time, plus execution counts and an instance pulse every 6 hours.

disable.name: N8N_TEMPLATES_ENABLED
disable.note: Stops workflow template fetching. Templates stop working in the UI.

apps.notes: The docs do not name the destination hosts, so none are listed.

apps.name: Netdata
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous system, configuration and alert/chart count data on agent start, stop and fatal errors, plus product usage events from the dashboard.
apps.notes: The docs name a Netdata cloud function and PostHog as the receivers but give no hostnames, so no destination is listed.

apps.name: Nextcloud
apps.what_is_sent: If the usage survey is active, an app list, database type and size, encryption status, share counts, PHP settings, server details and usage statistics.
apps.notes: Unverified. Nextcloud's usage survey app sends anonymized data to Nextcloud and can be disabled at any time, but its page does not say whether it is active by default, where the data goes or how to turn it off.

apps.name: NocoDB
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymous usage data.
apps.notes: Unverified. The docs say NC_DISABLE_TELE disables telemetry and ask you to keep telemetry on, which implies it is on by default, but they state neither the default nor the value to set. "true" is an assumption.

apps.name: Novu
apps.what_is_sent: Usage statistics such as event, integration, organization, subscriber, topic, user and workflow counts.
apps.still_sent: An hourly keep-alive ping (hostname, instance ID, IP address, platform, release, memory figures) is sent whether telemetry is on or off.

disable.instructions: Telemetry can also be turned off in the Admin Settings.

apps.notes: Unverified. The docs do not state the default, do not name the destination host, and do not say which container reads NOVU_TELEMETRY. The official compose file and env example do not set the variable either.

apps.name: OneCLI
apps.notes: The docs say self-hosted OneCLI (Community and Enterprise) sends no telemetry to OneCLI or any third party, and that there is nothing to opt out of. The gateway's analytics only run if both POSTHOG_API_KEY and POSTHOG_HOST are set, and neither has a default.

apps.name: OpenSEO
apps.what_is_sent: A self_host.heartbeat event with an install ID, version, deploy target, database backend and aggregate counts such as users and projects.

disable.name: OPENSEO_TELEMETRY_DISABLED
disable.note: Any value other than 0, false, no or off opts out. Those four keep telemetry on.

apps.notes: Taken from the project source. The README and Docker self-hosting guide do not mention telemetry.

apps.name: Outline
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymized statistics, sent to the maintainers as part of the check for updates.
apps.notes: The official sample env file ships with ENABLE_UPDATES=true. It does not name the destination host. Error tracking through Sentry is separate and only active if you set SENTRY_DSN.

apps.name: Portainer
apps.notes: Portainer no longer collects anonymous usage statistics. The Matomo integration was removed in version 2.38.0. Before that, statistics were collected only when users explicitly opted in.

apps.name: PostHog (self-hosted)
apps.what_is_sent: Product usage data, sent to PostHog.

disable.name: OPT_OUT_CAPTURE
disable.note: Set it on the web container and on the workers. The official compose file passes it to both for that reason.

apps.notes: OPT_OUT_CAPTURE defaults to False. The docs do not name the destination host. The hobby compose file takes its image from REGISTRY_URL, which the deploy script sets to posthog/posthog.

apps.name: PowerSync Service
apps.what_is_sent: Usage counters and gauges such as bytes synced and replication lag, collected every few minutes and tied to a random instance UUID.
apps.notes: The docs say the metrics go to PowerSync without naming a host. The opt-out is a config key, so phonehome cannot write a fix for it.

apps.name: Qdrant
apps.what_is_sent: Anonymized system information, performance timings and counters, and critical error reports such as backtraces.
apps.notes: The docs page does not name the destination host.

apps.name: Sentry (self-hosted)
apps.what_is_sent: The beacon sends an installation ID, the Sentry version, general anonymous statistics on the data pattern and the names and versions of installed Python modules. A contact email only if you opt in to that.

disable.instructions: Self-hosted issue reporting (OS username, IP address, install log, runtime errors and performance data) is a separate choice the installer asks for. Set REPORT_SELF_HOSTED_ISSUES=0 or pass --no-report-self-hosted-issues to install.sh.

apps.notes: The official page contradicts itself on the default. One section says Sentry sends anonymous usage statistics by default, another says the beacon is used if you opt in. The default is recorded as unknown for that reason. The beacon server is run by the Sentry team. The page does not give its hostname. sentry-self-hosted-local is the name the official compose file gives the image it builds locally from the Sentry image.

apps.name: SigNoz
apps.what_is_sent: Deployment platform, OS, build version and variant, counts of dashboards, alerts and users, and ingested data volume. User emails too unless identity collection is turned off.

disable.instructions: v0.88.0 and later: set statsreporter.enabled to false in the SigNoz configuration. To keep reporting but drop emails, set statsreporter.collect.identities to false.
Before v0.88.0: set TELEMETRY_ENABLED=false in the query-service environment and restart query-service.

apps.notes: The opt-out depends on the version, so phonehome does not write a fix for it. The docs do not name the destination host.

apps.name: Supabase (self-hosted)
apps.notes: The docs say self-hosted Supabase does not phone home or collect any telemetry. The Supabase CLI is a separate tool and does collect usage telemetry, with its own opt-out.

apps.name: TimescaleDB
apps.what_is_sent: An anonymous JSON usage report with the instance's versions, operating system, database feature counts and job statistics.
apps.notes: The default telemetry level is "basic". The opt-out is a PostgreSQL setting, so phonehome cannot write a fix for it. The docs page does not name the destination host.

apps.name: Traefik
apps.what_is_sent: Only after you opt in with sendAnonymousUsage. The Traefik version, a hash of the configuration and an anonymized static configuration.
apps.notes: Anonymous usage data needs an explicit opt-in (global.sendAnonymousUsage). Separately, the version check (global.checkNewVersion) is on by default and sends the running version and the public IP to update.traefik.io. Turn that off in the static configuration if you do not want it.

apps.name: Umami
apps.what_is_sent: Completely anonymous telemetry data, according to the docs. They give no further detail.

disable.name: DISABLE_UPDATES
disable.note: Stops the check for new Umami versions.

apps.notes: The docs describe telemetry as something you can choose to disable. They do not use the word "default" or name the destination host.

apps.name: Weaviate
apps.what_is_sent: Server version, OS and architecture, module names, object and collection counts, cluster details and client library usage. No data objects, collection names or property names.
